chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Do you consider that if a man were to enter the state of Ihram at the end of a prescribed prayer, would that suffice him?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُجْزِئُهُ: would suffice him / be valid for him

ai.seo_question: Is it valid to enter Ihram right after finishing a prayer?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the immediate transition from a prescribed prayer to the state of Ihram, emphasizing the simplicity and flexibility of ritual consecration. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that Ihram is not bound to a specific time slot but is valid upon the intention and declaration following any obligatory act, provided the prerequisites are met. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the procedural ease of entering the sacred state during Hajj or Umrah.
